cw-story.text: Treat Crimson Warden as a lived-in carrier workplace rather than a floating throne or generic warship. Every page should show cause-and-effect among launch, recovery, maintenance, medicine, rescue, command and civilian need. Human-scale acting comes first. The ship can be visually immense, but decisions land through people doing jobs.

cw-carrier-ops.text: Carrier operations must remain spatially legible. Aircraft move through defined launch lanes, recovery approaches, elevators, maintenance bays and safety zones. Deck crews communicate with hand signals, headsets and physical movement. Damage changes what the deck can do next. Avoid random crowds standing near moving craft or impossible instant turnarounds.

cw-ember-burden.text: Ember doctrine appears as the burden of authority: commanders decide when costs are justified and own consequences they cannot personally absorb. Avoid speeches praising sacrifice, authoritarian glamour, literal fire symbolism in every frame, crowns or throne imagery. Mature Fleet design remains blue, gold and Ion White with restrained ember-crimson lineage accents.

cw-combat-clarity.text: Space action must be readable as geography and choices. Establish relative positions, objectives, fuel/time limits and which craft are protecting civilians, recovering pilots or threatening the carrier. Do not reduce combat to abstract laser clutter. Unmarked raiders are one splinter group, not visual shorthand for all Shards.

cw-aftermath.text: After action, remain with labor and absence: triage, cleanup, damage tags, tool counts, empty stations, repairs and the next tasking order. Do not convert loss into a triumphant memorial pose. The emotional point is that operations continue because people continue the work.
